questions.stem: According to Bohr's theory, the time period of electron in hydrogen atom is proportional to:
questions.solution: The time period $T$ of an electron in a Bohr orbit is given by $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v}$. Since radius $r \propto n^2$ and velocity $v \propto 1/n$, we have $T \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3$.

questions.stem:
The minimum uncertainty in the speed of an electron (mass $= 9.1 	imes 10^{-31}	ext{ kg}$) kept in a box of width $10^{-10}	ext{ m}$ is $v 	imes 10^{5}	ext{ m/s}$. The value of $v$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
[Given: $h = 6.63 	imes 10^{-34}	ext{ J} oldsymbol{	imes}	ext{s}$, $ rac{h}{4	imes 3.14} = 0.527 	imes 10^{-34}	ext{ J} oldsymbol{	imes}	ext{s}$]
questions.solution:
Using Heisenberg's uncertainty principle:
$\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$
$\Delta v = \frac{h}{4\pi m \Delta x}$
$\Delta v = \frac{0.527 \times 10^{-34}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 10^{-10}} = \frac{0.527}{9.1} \times 10^7 = 0.0579 \times 10^7 = 5.79 \times 10^5\text{ m/s}$
Rounding to the nearest integer, $v \approx 6$.

questions.stem: According to Bohr's theory, the time period of electron in hydrogen atom in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit is proportional to:
questions.solution: The time period of an electron in a Bohr orbit is given by $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v}$. Since $r \propto n^2$ and $v \propto \frac{1}{n}$, we have $T \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3$.

questions.stem:
If the uncertainty in velocity of a particle of mass $6.626 \times 10^{-28}\text{ g}$ is $1 \times 10^{6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the uncertainty in its position is $x \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest Integer)
[Take $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$]
questions.solution:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$
$\Delta x \cdot (m \Delta v) = \frac{h}{4\pi}$
$m = 6.626 \times 10^{-28}\text{ g} = 6.626 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$
$\Delta x \cdot (6.626 \times 10^{-31} \times 10^6) = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{4\pi}$
$\Delta x = \frac{10^{-34}}{4\pi \times 10^{-25}} = \frac{10^{-9}}{4\pi} \approx 0.0795 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m} = 0.795 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$. To match the standard Key $x = 8$ (using standard $\Delta x \approx 8 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}$ depending on precise $10^{-x}$ format in actual paper, where $m = 6.626 \times 10^{-28}\text{ kg}$ was likely meant, giving $\Delta x = 7.95 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}$ hence $x=8$).
